newsitem.title: GERMANY: Rescue plan for Germany's SKET seen by year end.
newsitem.headline: Rescue plan for Germany's SKET seen by year end.

text.p: A new rescue plan for struggling east German machinery maker SKET GmbH should be drawn up by the end of this year and submitted for approval to the European Union, officials said.
SKET management, the state government of Lower Saxony and the BvS state agency want to improve the chances of privatising SKET through the plan, they said in a joint statement.
Management opened liquidation proceedings earlier this week after its 1,850 workforce refused to support a drastic cost-cutting programme under which two thirds of them would lose their jobs.
SKET once employed 18,000 workers as a main supply to communist eastern Europe but its losses have soaked up over a billion marks in state aid since Germany was unified in 1990.

Bonn came under opposition fire in parliament on Friday from the reformed east German communist PDS, which called a debate on SKET, and the Social Democrats (SPD) who accused it of going back on promises to save SKET.

Economics Minister Guenter Rexrodt said management had no choice but to open liquidation proceedings after workers refused to back the new cost cuts. SKET missed targets from an earlier rescue plan set last April, he said.

Helmut Buettner, of Chancellor Helmut Kohl's Christian Democrats (CDU), said liquidation would be a "last chance" for SKET, which expects to lose 190 million marks this year on turnover of 120 million marks.

BvS president Heinrich Horneg and SKET board members will go on Monday to Brussels for talks with European Union competition commissioner Karel Van Miert to discuss the main points of the rescue plan, a BvS spokesman said.
The BvS will then meet next Wednesday with the receivers handling the liquidation of SKET. Under east German law the process is a mixture of bankruptcy and creditor settlement.
Work will also continue to secure a 100 million mark order from Vietnam to keep SKET's Magdeburg plant working, the BvS said.
